source.snippet: The portfolio math. When 30 small apps beat 1 big one. For a decade the indie hacker... [score 22, 3 comments, tags: indiehackers, startup, productivity, webdev]

problem_statement: Indie hackers and solo founders building a portfolio of small apps lack tooling to manage, monitor revenue/metrics, and cross-promote multiple micro-products from a single dashboard, forcing them to juggle many separate admin panels and spreadsheets.
target_segment: Indie hackers and solo operators running 3-30 small SaaS or digital products simultaneously, typically generating $500–$10k MRR across the portfolio.
notes: Score 22 with 3 comments; topic resonates in indie-hacker community. Paying-buyer evidence: these operators already pay for hosting, analytics, and email tools per product — a consolidated portfolio management layer with unified metrics, renewal alerts, and cross-promotion scheduling would command $29-99/month. Comparable tools (Makerlog, Indie Hackers analytics) are weak on the multi-product management angle.
